motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Token landing. Reduced motion fades instead.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Honey pill for the single primary action.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: oklch(0.5 0.145 58); color: oklch(1 0 0); border: 0; border-radius: 999px; padding: 12px 22px; font-family: Schibsted Grotesk, sans-serif; font-weight: 600; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: oklch(0.44 0.14 58); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid oklch(0.5 0.145 58); outline-offset: 3px; }

narrative.overview: Two classmates lean over one machine in a bright classroom. The page is that laptop: white daylight, ink, and a single saturated honey that is the arena they are racing inside.
keyCharacteristics: One honey field does the shouting. White and ink do the reading.
Levels are a vertical path, a real sequence, never a card grid.
Panels are flat, framed with a 2px ink line, radius at most 16px.
Controls are pills. The arena rows are full-bleed, not tiles.
Motion is a short ease-out stagger when tokens land. Reduced motion fades.

rules.name: The One Arena Rule
rules.body: Honey is a region, not a highlight. If a screen has no race to point at, honey stays on the single primary action.

rules.name: The Code Face Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono is for selectors, properties, values, and 0-1-2-1. UI words stay in the grotesque.

dos: Do keep honey on the arena, the current station, and the primary action.
donts: Don't use a dark code-editor theme, a cream or sand page, or a grid of identical level cards.
Don't use gradient text, glassmorphism, side-stripe borders, eyebrow labels above headings, or hero-metric XP blocks.
